_: VPcmFloModem's constructor: six member objects, one of which is an entire
V90Modem and another an entire V92Modem, four calls whose arguments are
all immediates, three memsets and thirty constant stores.
THE INTERESTING DEFECTS ARE ALL WIRING.  Six arguments reach eleven
places between them and two of the eleven take the SAME address --
`&this->dil` goes to the V90Modem's third slot and the V92Modem's
fourth -- so the class of mistake this file exists to catch is an
argument landing in a neighbouring slot, not a wrong number.
TWO OF THESE ARE CAUGHT IN A WORD THAT CAN NEVER COMPARE EQUAL, and that
is the point worth stating.  `GenericIIR` BORROWS its coefficient
arrays, so the entrance filter holds two pointers to static tables: ours
into our .data and the blob's into its own.  A comparison that merely
excluded them would let a swap of `entFiltDen` and `entFiltNum` through,
which is exactly findings 1301 and 1307's shape.  t_vpcmctor.cpp instead
pins each word to a NAMED symbol on each side AND checks that the two
targets are byte-identical over the filter's own declared order, so the
swap fails twice over.  Verified by making the swap and watching both
checks fire.
THE STORES THE CONSTRUCTOR MAKES THAT `VPCMXF_Create` IMMEDIATELY
CONTRADICTS are mutated here as well -- `nofBitsPerSymbol` 0 against its
2, `minNofTransmitSequences` 0 against its 1, `v34BaudAllow` all ones
against its {1,0,1,1,1,0}.  Those are only observable in the direct
constructor sweep, because a modem that came out of `VPCMXF_Create`
never has the constructor's values for them.
